notes.text: The author numbers this sheet 34 and heads it with underlined item 15, Introduction des proespaces. The pale bottom-left 76 is foliation in another unnamed hand and is represented separately.

The manuscript designates a tubular provoisinage for the written X_i star complement and labels display (51) an équivalence d’homo- / topie des|de proespaces. The raised marks on the V symbols are overdrawn; their glyph and strike states remain local doubts. These sentences report the manuscript and do not certify its mathematical claims.

The author introduces the i<j line and writes the intersection display (52). Its first base contains superposed X and V strokes with one shared ij. The intersection expression was not used to infer which layer is live. The diagram has a horizontal b_ij hook and a downward s_ij hook, with the lower Xi expression, a w|h label, one tilde and two opposite arrow marks. The closing parenthesis is visibly before V_i.

The oblique left marginal question begins Pour un and asks est-ce une équivalence d’homotopie ?. Its formula contains a doubtful raised b and ends at a hooked connector without written target letters. The manuscript’s question is preserved as a question; no proof check of it was undertaken.

The right NB relates its written V_i intersection V_j equals slashed-circle formula to the words i et j ne sont pas comparables. Its long insertion leader attaches the parenthesis du moins si les ouverts de X sont normaux, p.ex. X métrisable to that clause. The note also writes V_ii=V_i. These are attributed manuscript statements, with no independent result asserted here.

Display (53) and its following sentence present X as the author’s colimit/recollement expression. The vertical crossed brace-like glyph before b_ij is retained with state doubt; it was not replaced by a mathematically expected pair of arrows.

Display (54) gives the author’s multi-index intersection notation, followed by a drapeau line. The bottom NB is transcribed literally, including = for the written même abbreviation, l’ens., braces, one continuation dash, ne forme pas un drapeau, and mais il est vide. The varied continuation marks in the heading, (54), the flag and the note were read separately.

All first-pass reading decisions on this page were based on visible strokes and the supplied witness collation. No theorem, categorical identification, or conditional claim was proved or introduced. check_events is empty because transcription reading alone was not treated as mathematical verification.

The repeated curved V bases have no independent alphabet contrast established on this sheet. Plain V leads only as a typographic candidate and calligraphic V remains visible in the doubt alternatives. Two tiny pale marks near the upper-left start of the lower V in the recollement caption have uncertain provenance; no extra accent or prime is assigned. The final V in (54) is retraced without an independently recoverable cancelled letter.
